answer: An agent marketplace can view identity through the prism of locked collateral: every active account must escrow $100 for 30 days before bidding on jobs. A whisper of reputation cannot waive that rule, and each new identity starts the same voyage through the lockup. An attacker running 10,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize $1 million; creating more names does not create more bidding power without committing more capital.
